deities: Durga (as Maa Biraja / Viraja / Girija, dwibhuja Mahishasuramardini)

history.period: Present temple 13th century AD (Somavamsi rule); idol venerated reportedly from the 5th century (unverified); destroyed 1568 AD, rebuilt early 19th century
history.summary: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas: per Tantra Chudamani and Puranic tradition, the navel (nabhi) of Goddess Sati fell here, making Jajpur 'Nabhi Gaya' and the town historically 'Viraja Kshetra' (Jajpur's name traces back to it). The present temple was built in the 13th century by the Somavamsi/Keshari king Jajati (Yayati) Keshari, destroyed during the Afghan conquest in 1568 AD, and reconstructed/repaired in the early 19th century by Jajpur zamindar Sudarshan Mohapatra. The presiding dwibhuja (two-armed) Durga idol spears Mahishasura's chest with one hand and pulls the buffalo-demon's tail with the other; her crown bears Ganesha, a crescent moon, and a lingam. It is the only Shakti Peetha where pitru puja/pinda daan (shradha rites for ancestors) is regularly performed, and the compound holds 108 Shiva lingas.

name: Maa Biraja Temple
town_description: Jajpur is one of Odisha's most historic towns, on the banks of the Baitarani (Vaitarani) river about 125 km north of Bhubaneswar. It was the capital of the Somavamsi (Keshari) kingdom and is steeped in Shakti and Shaiva heritage - the name 'Jajpur' itself derives from 'Viraja Kshetra', the sacred seat of Goddess Biraja. Jajpur district is famed for its dense concentration of temples and Shiva lingas.
